module.title: Distributions versus summaries
module.course: DA-730: Clinical Data Visualization and Decision Storytelling

source.curriculum_title: DA-730 Course Redesign: Analyzing, Visualizing, and Storytelling with Data
source.note: The public CMS OP_18b hospital median anchors only the discharged center. Every encounter, pathway shape, trend, disposition, and boarding mechanism remains synthetic teaching data.

contributors.name: OpenAI Codex
contributors.role: module reconciliation, public-source calibration, specification, and technical checks

technical_validation.evidence: The real variant passed 26 of 26 checks. Null and trivial variants each passed 23 of 23 checks. Four lab figures, a monthly table, and three critique figures rendered successfully.

validation.determinism: Same calibration, variant, and seed produce byte-identical encounter files.
validation.calibration_build: 4,658 OP_18b rows, including 4,081 reported and 577 unavailable values.
validation.lab_execution: pass: four PNGs and one monthly metrics CSV

hidden_process_visual_preview.observation: The admitted density has a lower-stay process and a distinct boarded mode near 782 minutes; pooling weakens the longer-stay mode.

known_issues: Human visualization, emergency department, accessibility, and independent-instructor reviews are pending.
CMS OP_18b is a hospital-level median and does not provide a patient-level distribution.
Only the discharged median center is calibrated to the public source; all other encounter and pathway behavior is synthetic.
Acuity and age group are assigned independently of length of stay and must not be used for clinical inference.
The model omits staffing, occupancy, seasonality, transfers, censoring, return visits, and other real emergency department processes.
Technical execution has been tested on Windows; macOS and Linux clean-run verification remains pending.
